svg.title: The bakery temperature ladder: the temperatures a boulanger measures, from freezer to oven
svg.desc: A vertical ladder, not to scale, from the coldest at the bottom to the hottest at the top. Minus 18 degrees: freezer. 0 to 4 degrees: cold room for fresh yeast and pâte fermentée; 2 to 6 degrees for pointage retardé. About 13 degrees: butter at lamination. 18 to 22 degrees: croissant détrempe after mixing. Fournil air: measured at every batch. 22 to 26 degrees: dough at the end of mixing, depending on the product. 24 to 28 degrees and 75 to 85 percent humidity: apprêt. About 35 degrees: fastest gas from yeast but poorer flavour. 40 degrees: the maximum for water poured on yeast. 46 to 50 degrees: yeast dies in the dough early in baking. At least 90 degrees: core of a baked loaf. 230 to 250 degrees: oven.

g.text: The bakery temperature ladder (not to scale)
Each rung is a temperature you measure or control; your fiche technique gives the exact figure
at least 90 °C
40 °C maximum
about 35 °C
measure it
about 13 °C
Oven: 250 °C deck (PC-02); home oven checked with an oven thermometer
Core of a baked loaf (température à cœur), read with a probe
Yeast dies in the dough, early in baking
Water poured on yeast: never hotter
Yeast makes gas fastest, but flavour and dough control suffer
Apprêt in the chambre de pousse (PC-02: 25 °C, 75-80 % HR)
Dough at the end of mixing (TPV): 23-25 °C for pain courant
Fournil air and flour: not set by you, but they change the water
Croissant détrempe after mixing (kept cool for lamination)
Butter at lamination (beurre de tourage): cold but bendable
Cold room: fresh yeast, pâte fermentée; pointage retardé 2-6 °C
Freezer: frozen doughs and products
Sources: formulas and lessons 02.6, 04.4, 04.6 of this course; King Arthur Baking (core and butter temperatures). Ranges, not fixed values.
